mutation_targets.rationale: Clearing the auth boundary lets the model invent a successful operation with authenticated=False, which is exactly what AuthRequiredEverywhere is supposed to forbid.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_AuthBypass { some op: Operation | op.outcome = Success and op.authenticated = False }

mutation_targets.rationale: Clearing the uniqueness constraints lets two TaskDeletion entries reference the same task, which is the canonical violation of an append-only log and permanent deletion.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_AppendOnlyViolation { some disj d1, d2: TaskDeletion | d1.deletedTask = d2.deletedTask }

mutation_targets.rationale: Clearing audit completeness lets a successful delete op exist with no corresponding log entry, breaking the per-delete one-to-one audit invariant.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_MissingDeletionLog { some op: Operation | op.kind = OpDelete and op.outcome = Success and (no d: TaskDeletion | d.producedByOp = op) }

mutation_targets.rationale: Clearing the attribution fact lets a log entry record a deleter different from the actual op caller — exactly the misattribution case the assertion is designed to detect.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_WrongDeleter { some d: TaskDeletion | d.deletedBy != d.producedByOp.caller }

mutation_targets.rationale: Clearing the identity-from-context fact lets a task's recorded creator diverge from its create-op's authenticated caller, modelling the payload-spoofing bug FR-002 forbids.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_SpoofedCreator { some t: Task | t.creator != t.createdByOp.caller }

mutation_targets.rationale: Clearing the closed-task edit rule lets a successful edit on a Done task keep the status as Done, which is precisely the PATCH-on-closed bug FR-011 forbids.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_EditClosedNoReopen { some op: Operation | op.kind = OpEdit and op.outcome = Success and op.preStatus = Done and op.setsStatus = Done }
